answer:
The simulation models spray combustion of liquid n-dodecane injected into hot air in a cylindrical combustion chamber, solved with OpenFOAM.
The solver is reactingParcelFoam, coupling the Lagrangian evaporating spray with the reacting turbulent gas phase.
The domain is a 2D axisymmetric half-plane of a cylinder, 0.2 m long (axial direction) and 0.1 m in diameter (radial direction).
The mesh is generated with blockMesh using a 100x50 grid: 100 cells in the axial direction and 50 cells in the radial direction, with grading that concentrates cells near the axis and near the injector face.
The chamber axis is modeled with the 'axis' boundary type as the symmetry centreline.
The inlet is a velocity-specified co-flow air inlet at the upstream face with U = (10 0 0) m/s, temperature 800 K, pressure 101325 Pa, and species mass fractions O2 = 0.233 and N2 = 0.767.
The initial condition in the entire chamber at t=0 is hot air at rest (U = 0) at 800 K and 101325 Pa with the same O2/N2 composition.
The outlet at the downstream end is an ambient outlet at 101325 Pa using a totalPressure boundary condition for pressure, with zeroGradient boundary conditions for velocity, temperature, and all species so flow can enter or leave as needed.
The cylinder walls use a noSlip velocity condition and a fixed wall temperature of 400 K, so heat is lost from the gas to the cooler walls.
The spray is a liquid n-dodecane (nC12H26) cone injection located on the axis at the centre of the inlet face.
The liquid dodecane is injected at 300 K with a total mass flow rate of 0.002 kg/s.
The droplet size distribution is Rosin-Rammler with a mean diameter of 50e-6 m (50 microns); a cone half-angle of 15 degrees is used as a typical value, and the parcel injection rate is chosen so the total mass flow equals 0.002 kg/s.
Droplet heat and mass transfer use the RanzMarshall model and droplet drag uses the standard drag model.
Turbulence is modeled with the k-epsilon model.
Gas-phase combustion uses finite-rate chemistry with a two-step global reaction mechanism for n-dodecane, where the first step converts C12H26 to CO and smaller hydrocarbon fragments and the second step converts CO to CO2, with rate constants selected as reasonable values for a two-step global dodecane scheme.
Thermodynamic data for all species use the janaf format.
The combustion model and reaction scheme are configured in constant/combustionProperties and constant/reactionSchemes.
The case is run to a steady burning state, using a simulation end time and time-step control (Courant number limiting) chosen to keep the transient spray combustion calculation stable.
